clue.text: Damn brilliant?

definitions.meaning: an exasperated intensifier, as in 'that blasted car'

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one word: the mild British expletive and the literal 'ablaze'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses: a mild British swear word used as an intensifier, and blazing with bright light.

clue.text: Overweight insect embodying a pair of insects, might you say?

indicators.note: the insect takes the other piece into its body

parts.note: a fly is an insect

indicators.note: the phrase is heard as the letters it sounds like

parts.note: a pair of bees, heard as A and two letter Bs

explanation.surface: A fat insect with two more insects inside it, as you might describe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pair of insects' is spoken as 'a pair of bees', which sounds like A, B, B; 'embodying' puts those inside FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby describes soft, sagging flesh, typical of someone carrying excess weight.

clue.text: Nerves, small quantity within muscles

indicators.note: the small amount goes inside the muscles

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles
a dab is a small amount

explanation.surface: A jittery person has a dab of tension in the stomach muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang, as in 'the screaming abdabs', for a fit of nervous anxiety or jitters.

clue.text: Guardian spies (no lie) out to steal Times leader — that's corporate skulduggery

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order and rearranged
the opening letter of the newspaper's name is taken

explanation.surface: Guardian spies, honestly, set out to steal from a rival Times editorial: dirty business dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to steal' signals that the T from 'Times leader' joins the scrambled letters of GUARDIAN SPIES NO LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying by one company on another's trade secrets is underhand corporate behaviour.

clue.text: Bloke biting tail of huge, agile carnivore

indicators.note: the man takes the letter between his teeth, inside him

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a bloke

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A man bites the tail of a huge, nimble meat-eating beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender, cat-like mammal related to civets, hunting small prey, is a nimble meat-eater.

clue.text: Award lower degree after third from London?

indicators.note: the degree is placed following the letters taken from the city

parts.note: to dip something is to lower it

indicators.note: the opening third of a six-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a lesser degree is handed out to a student who came third in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third from London' is not the third letter but a third of the word: its first two letters, LO.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate awarded on completing a course of study is a common kind of award.

clue.text: More compact packing is preferable, primarily, for pharmacist

indicators.note: the denser word has the rest packed into it

parts.note: denser means more compact
taken as written

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A chemist advises that more compact packing is better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packing' reads as luggage, but it signals one piece holding the others; the pharmacist is the one who hands out medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist who makes up and hands out medicines is one who dispenses them.

clue.text: Innocent, possibly, as a satirist

definitions.meaning: Innocent was the name of thirteen Roman pontiffs
Alexander ... wrote satirical verse such as The Dunciad

explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent' reads as an adjective, but it is a papal name.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of the Catholic Church, several called Innocent, shares a surname with the poet Alexander Pope, a celebrated satirist.

clue.text: Stranger diet, sour balls

indicators.note: balls means nonsense, a mess, so the letters are made a mess of

explanation.surface: An odd diet of sour balls, perhaps sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like 'more strange' but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not belonging to a group, an unfamiliar person, is a synonym of stranger.

clue.text: All the possibilities in a US state, fine and good

parts.note: NY is New York
thin means fine, as in a fine thread

explanation.surface: Every option is open in a fine, good American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'whatever' or 'everything is possible' covers every option there is.

clue.text: Given support as in difficulties, evidently distressing on every front

indicators.note: each word's front, its opening letter, is taken in turn

explanation.surface: Someone helped through hard times, plainly upsetting from all sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone is to help or support them; the past participle matches 'given support'.

clue.text: Pose altered wearing absurd theatrical make-up

indicators.note: the outer word has the other on, so it goes around it

parts.note: nutty means crazy or absurd

indicators.note: the letters of the word pose are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A changed stance looks silly when worn with ridiculous stage make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' sounds like clothing, but it means one piece goes around the scrambled other.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a mouldable putty actors apply to reshape their noses on stage, a kind of stage cosmetic.

clue.text: Responsible adult resentful — minding hell for the most part?

indicators.note: the bitter word looks after, holds, the trimmed one inside it

parts.note: bitter means resentful

indicators.note: most of the word is used, the last letter dropped

parts.note: the abyss is the bottomless pit of hell

explanation.surface: A grown-up in charge is bitter about looking after a hellish situation, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark nods to how hellish minding small children can feel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone minding children while parents are out is the grown-up left responsible for them.

clue.text: Possibly a Christmas cracker to pull thus contains letters on a pencil in red, say?

definitions.text: Possibly a Christmas cracker to pull

indicators.note: the thus-and-pencil piece goes inside the drink

parts.note: red is an example of wine

indicators.note: the short word holds the pencil letters within it

parts.note: so means thus
HB marks a pencil as hard-black, medium grade

explanation.surface: A festive party cracker seems to hold pencil lettering and red ink.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a paper party tube pulled apart by two people; the answer is the forked bird bone pulled the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked bird bone is pulled at Christmas dinner like a cracker, the bigger piece granting a wish.

clue.text: Just about survive seeing nurse possibly pocketing wad, unexpectedly

indicators.note: the nurse word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a nurse is one who treats patients, a treater

indicators.note: the letters of wad come out in a surprise order

explanation.surface: Barely getting by on seeing a nurse pocket a wad of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse possibly' is a definition by example: a nurse is someone who treats patients.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to stay afloat without making progress, merely surviving.

clue.text: A lifesaver, as bloom catches showers

indicators.note: the flowering word takes the other inside it

parts.note: to burgeon is to flourish or bloom
rains are showers

explanation.surface: A garden saviour, as flowers flourish when it rains.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon operating on the brain is a doctor whose work often saves lives.

clue.text: Frightfully nice trait is involved

indicators.note: the letters are put into a frightful, jumbled order

explanation.surface: A frightfully pleasant quality is a complicated one.
explanation.definitionFit: An involved plot is complicated and full of detail, synonymous with intricate.

clue.text: Unblinking female lacking features on the head?

parts.note: without ears, the features on the sides of the head

explanation.surface: A woman with a fixed stare whose face lacks features?
explanation.definitionFit: Unblinking describes facing danger without flinching, being brave and unafraid.

clue.text: Group claiming tycoon is a harlot

indicators.note: the group takes in the businessman

parts.note: a set is a group
Donald Trump is a property tycoon

explanation.surface: A group's allegation that a business magnate is a loose woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic, insulting word for a prostitute or promiscuous woman, synonymous with harlot.

clue.text: A sucker, one who is no longer in love with farming?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, someone who no longer is one
a tractor fan adores farm machinery

explanation.surface: A gullible person, or a jilted lover who has gone off farm life?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'sucker' as a dupe; it means a device that draws air out.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen or bathroom ventilator pulls out stale air, so it literally sucks.

clue.text: Capital once cut, reported shortly as showing little growth

indicators.note: the city name loses its last letter

parts.note: Bonn was the capital of West Germany

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: said means reported

explanation.surface: A former capital's growth was cut, reportedly showing little expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature tree is grown in a pot and pruned to keep it tiny, so its growth is stunted.

clue.text: Item no longer in pubs, hard to lose — is lost!

indicators.note: the hard letter is dropped from the item

parts.note: ashtrays vanished from pubs with the smoking ban
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A pub item, gone with the smoking ban and hard to lose, is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has wandered off course or gone missing, as lost things do.

clue.text: Embarrassing defeat, as swimmer drops head

indicators.note: the fish name loses its first letter

parts.note: a trout is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A swimmer losing a race badly hangs their head in shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing, one-sided defeat, which is humiliating for the loser.

clue.text: Wild thing joining clubs as a swinger?

indicators.note: the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: a tiger is a wild animal
woods are golf clubs

explanation.surface: A wild party animal joins clubs as a swinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinger' suggests a partygoer, but it means one who swings a golf club: the champion golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous golfer swings clubs for a living, so he is a swinger in the golfing sense.

clue.text: Occurrence where detainee finally gets let out

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: to vent is to let out, as steam or anger

explanation.surface: A happening in which a prisoner is at last released.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is something that happens, a synonym of occurrence.

clue.text: See 12
See 3
Spraying of tear gas ultimately a shocking police tactic?

indicators.note: spraying scatters, so the letters are scattered into a new order
only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Riot police spray tear gas, perhaps a shocking tactic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives S from 'gas', mixed with TEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use this stun gun to deliver an electric shock and subdue a suspect.

clue.text: That will teach you maths, other examples to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A teacher sets maths and more examples, as a lesson to the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloating idiom said when someone gets their comeuppance, equivalent to 'serves you right'.

clue.text: Shock provided inside nappy material

indicators.note: the conditional word goes within the cloth

parts.note: terry towelling is the looped cotton used for cloth nappies (diapers)
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Something alarming hidden inside a baby's nappy.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone is to frighten or alarm them badly, a verb synonym.
